title: Form 10-IEA: Why Business Taxpayers Can't Switch Regimes Annually
description: Taxpayers with income from a business or profession face restrictions on frequently switching between the old and new tax regimes. To opt for the new tax regi.

faq.a: Form 10-IEA is used by individuals and HUFs with business or professional income to declare their choice of opting into or out of the new tax regime (Section 115BAC) for an assessment year.
Only individuals and Hindu Undivided Families (HUFs) who have income from a business or profession and wish to exercise or withdraw their option under Section 115BAC need to file this form.

faq.q: What is the deadline to file Form 10-IEA?
faq.a: The form must be filed on or before the due date for filing your Income Tax Return (ITR) for the relevant assessment year.

faq.q: Can I switch between regimes every year if I have business income?
faq.a: No, if you have business or professional income, you cannot switch between the old and new tax regimes every year. You can opt out of the new regime only once in your lifetime. If you re-enter the new regime after opting out, you cannot switch back to the old regime again.

faq.q: What happens if I stop having business income?
faq.a: If you cease to have any business or professional income, the restrictions imposed by Form 10-IEA no longer apply to you. You can then choose between the old and new regimes annually, like any other taxpayer without business income.

faq.q: Is Form 10-IEA required for salaried individuals?
faq.a: No, Form 10-IEA is not required for salaried individuals or those without business or professional income. They can choose their preferred tax regime directly in their ITR form each year without any restrictions on switching.
Form 10-IEA must be filed online through the official e-filing portal of the Income Tax Department (incometax.gov.in) by navigating to the 'e-File' section and selecting 'Income Tax Forms'.
